clarification: Requested before new subject calls: make the primary outcome a deterministic end-to-end benchmark score. Numeric anchors, metric units and target weights are unchanged. Completed submission failures receive zero index credit, without inventing raw capability scores. Held, unstarted and infrastructure-invalid outcomes remain unscored.
historical: Closed cohorts retain their original statuses, raw nulls, protocol and primary interpretations. Their v1.1 posthoc capability bounds can remain in details. Do not silently recast old infrastructure/numerical-gate failures as v1.2 model failures or relabel earlier cohorts as fresh control arms.
interpretation: Defined end-to-end benchmark index; not fraction of intelligence, pure artifact capability, proof of cross-cohort comparability, or a guarantee of server-level deterministic model generation.

name: WeightBench end-to-end score

paired_gain.scope: same fixed requested writer, target/draw allocation and matched fresh arms; scalar only when both arms have complete scoreable outcomes

primary.aggregation: Arithmetic mean over every prespecified draw per target, then equal one-third weight for each target. No valid-only denominator, no best draw, no averaging only the targets that ran.
primary.classification_gate: Common protocol must enumerate source-event-to-status rules and freeze mock cases before first subject. Both leads must use the identical registered map; do not invent per-outcome exemptions.
primary.determinism: Fixed artifact, evaluator/runtime, test items and episode seeds determine the reported point estimate subject to the stated runtime reproducibility qualification. Bootstrap/sample uncertainty does not replace the point estimate.
primary.failure_distinction: Ordinary request timeout after admitted execution and invalid action/schema output are end-to-end failures; explicit provider service/auth/quota errors, invalid admission, owned kernel/evaluator malfunction or lost artifact capture are infrastructure outcomes. Classify from frozen event rules and retained evidence, never from the achieved score. Unknown causes stay infrastructure/unresolved until evidence resolves them.
primary.meaning: Ability of the writer and its registered execution route to deliver valid useful weights within the fixed budget; not pure conditional artifact capability.
primary.overall_score: One 0–100 point value only when every allocated target/draw has a verified score or registered submission failure; otherwise null with coverage/status. No headline lower–upper range and no official rank of incomplete rows.
primary.paired_gain: One arithmetic difference when both complete arms have identical model/target/draw allocations; otherwise null.
primary.raw_scores: Preserve all original raw task results, verification statuses, failures and method evidence separately.

submission_failed.requires: A registered terminal reason plus retained attempt evidence. Failure consumes its allocated draw; no replacement, rescue or hidden drop.

primary.successful_submission: Use verified raw benchmark point estimates with the unchanged clipped normalization and weights.

primary_new: one pair per requested model per target; no writer-population CI or significant improvement claim from one paired replicate

secondary_capability_missing.display: incomplete index shown as lower–upper with weighted verified coverage; do not display lower alone as capability or rank incomplete rows
secondary_capability_missing.semantics: logical bounds on a hypothetical complete bounded index; not imputed scores, confidence intervals or population uncertainty

secondary_only: raw benchmark metrics and their intervals
operational submission counts and failure causes

secondary_paired_gain_bounds.scope: identical allocated model/target/draw cells; both arms fresh; report scalar only when both fully observed
secondary_paired_gain_bounds.unit: index points, not percent relative improvement
